title: Indian Banyan: Old Indian Banyans You Can Visit
meta_description: A banyan recruits its trunk from fused aerial roots. The Lahaina Banyan, planted in 1873, was scorched but not killed by the 2023 Maui fire.
intro: An Indian banyan does not grow a single trunk so much as recruit one. Aerial roots drop from its limbs, thicken into props where they reach the ground, and fuse with their neighbours into a mass that a tape measure reads as one continuous trunk, which is why the girth can run to absurd lengths without the tree being especially old. Brisbane's, in the City Botanic Gardens since the 1870s, measures 49 metres round. Singapore's in Tiong Bahru Park reached 22.8 metres of girth in under sixty years. Hawaii planted them in every town square. The Lahaina Banyan, set out in 1873 to mark fifty years of the town's first Protestant mission, grew sixteen trunks under a crown covering two thirds of an acre; the 2023 fire that destroyed the courthouse beside it scorched the tree and took much of its canopy, and it is still standing.
